scenario: [LECC.1.5]: a host-asserted `CallError` whose `code` does not match [LECC.1.2]'s pattern enters working memory with `code` = `internal.invariant` and every other slot as given; one that matches enters as given. Nine CallErrors, each with its own correlation (so none supersedes another, [LCRS.6.2.4]) and its own message, each asserted and pumped on its own, so the log order is the assert order. Malformed, one per way to break the pattern: c1 `Transport.timeout` (uppercase), c2 `transport-timeout` (a hyphen), c3 `.transport` (a leading dot), c4 `transport.` (a trailing dot), c5 `transport..timeout` (an empty segment), c6 `transport.9x` (a segment led by a digit), c7 `` (empty). Well-formed: c8 `transport.timeout`, and c9 `timeout_2`, one segment, which [LECC.1.5] admits though [LECC.1.3] forbids an adapter to send it. Rule `seen` logs each CallError's corr, code and message, so the log compares the rewrite and the pass-through of the other slots, not only that a rule fired. PATH PINNED: the CallError ingestion rewrite -- `wm.c`'s hook in `ds_engine_assert` calling `ds_error_code_valid` (`builtins.c`) (libds), `ds.engine.lecc_1_2_code_rewrite` (Mercury). The breaks: a rewrite that misses a class leaves that code in its line; one that also rewrites a well-formed or one-segment code puts `internal.invariant` in c8's or c9's; one that rebuilds the fact drops or changes a corr or message. NOT HERE: the `ds.errors.code_invariant_total` count, which no `expect.kind` reads ([RCTS.1.2.10]); it is libds's `test_nmet_4_1_inventory.c` and Mercury's scenario 107.
